note: KDWP state fishing lake at the north edge of Medicine Lodge in the Gyp Hills. KDWP allows camping throughout the area with no marked sites: campers use the gravel shore roads, turnarounds and points (a 2019 camper found most spots better for smaller units, with a couple of big ones on the loop across the lake). Group picnic shelter, two boat ramps (boats for fishing only) and a fishing dock; the northern 80 acres are open to hunting. --Claude
summary: KDWP page (Wayback 2026-07-11): camping allowed throughout the area, two pit toilets, group shelter, two ramps, dock; free and FCFS; max stay 7 nights under K.A.R. 115-8-9(c) (newly written). Phone 620-227-8609 -> manager 620-895-6446. Pin is in the water: move. Lakefront kept on the points' open aprons (soft).
flags: DESIGNATED CAMPING? KDWP's own page says 'Camping, picnicking, and fishing are allowed throughout the area' and marks no campsites; K.A.R. 115-8-9(a) allows camping 'only in designated areas ... as established by posted notice', so the area page itself is the designation (the whole area). On imagery the camping is along gravel shore roads with turnarounds and spurs on several points (east-shore point loop ~37.2984,-98.5799; spurs on the north-east and west shores), not a parking lot. A 5/2025 camper: 'It wasn't clear where the camp sites where'; 4/2019: 'sites were good for smaller units, but a couple big spots were found on the loop across'. Reads as agency-designated drive-in camping on maintained gravel roads (state, not wma), with no marked pads - a human may judge whether 'throughout the area' meets the designated-sites bar.
MAX STAY: newly written 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c)); the Barber page posts no other limit.
PHONE 620-227-8609 -> propose (620) 895-6446, the area manager on KDWP's Barber page (Pratt Operations Office 620-672-5911 is the regional line). apply.py doesn't write phone.

PIN MOVE: stored 37.2990,-98.5796 is in the lake, in the cove ~60-70 m north of the east-shore point. Propose 37.2984,-98.5799, the gravel turnaround loop on that point (the camping is spread around the lake; KDWP's east-side pit toilet is at 37.29660,-98.57888).

WATERFRONT 'lakefront' kept, soft: there are no designated pads, but on the east-shore point the gravel loop has an open bare-earth/grass apron 15-25 m wide outside the road down to the water, and spurs on the north-east and west shores run out to the shoreline - a rig can park with nothing but open ground between it and the lake. If AWH reads the loop road as the line, it drops to lakeview (both RV Life campers: 'Nice lake view', 'plenty of lake view'). Lake is roughly 60-80 acres on imagery (KDWP gives no acreage), well over the pond line.

WEBSITE as stored (KDWP page, 403 to plain HTTP; Wayback copy current to July 2026). HOOKUPS (none) and potable_water false left as stored (derived): the page doesn't mention water or electric; 2019/2025 campers report no hookups.
SAND: none - packed red-earth and gravel aprons on maintained gravel roads, not open-beach sand. No 4WD statement.
